cues.en: And what this means is that we are very nervous about technological risk,
cues.zh: 这意味着我们对技术风险极为敏感，

cues.en: Because there's no faster way to light yourself on fire than to write a piece of software that makes the same bad decision over and over in a tight loop. And as you make your systems faster and more effective and you increase your scope, you also increase the likelihood that you will incinerate yourself.
cues.zh: 因为要想自取灭亡，最快的办法莫过于写出一段在紧凑循环中反复做出相同错误决策的软件。随着你把系统做得更快、更高效，并且不断扩大规模，你把自己烧得粉身碎骨的可能性也随之剧增。

cues.en: So we are very careful about correctness of code. That's a kind of key
cues.zh: 所以我们非常重视代码的正确性。这是关键的

cues.en: motivator of the way that we approach things.
cues.zh: 推动因素，决定了我们处理问题的方式。

cues.zh: 而且

cues.zh: 我觉得，不同寻常的是，

cues.en: the primary way that we think about correctness, that we try and get to correctness, is
cues.zh: 我们思考正确性、努力实现正确性的主要方式，

cues.en: via trying to write code that is understandable and having strong practices of reading that code. So I think every software shop out there spends some amount of effort
cues.zh: 是通过尝试编写易于理解的代码，并建立强大的代码阅读实践。所以我认为，每家软件公司都会花一些精力

cues.en: reading code and some amount of effort testing code.
cues.zh: 阅读代码，也会花一些精力测试代码。

cues.en: But just as many people talk about test driven development,
cues.zh: 但正如很多人谈论测试驱动开发一样，

cues.en: I think if anything, are more like code review driven development. We worry a We think a lot about the point of view of the person who reads the code. And the reason for that is,
cues.zh: 我觉得如果真要说，更像是代码审查驱动开发。我们会很在意读代码的人怎么看。原因是，

cues.en: in a kind of financial setting, it's not the everyday condition that matters.
cues.zh: 在金融领域，日常情况并不重要。

cues.en: It's the weird thing that happens often in the tail of a distribution that doesn't happen very often, so it's hard to test for, but happens more often than you would have thought if you sort of imagined everything was a nice, fast decreasing normal distribution.
cues.zh: 真正重要的是分布尾部那些不常发生的异常情况。它们很难测试，但发生得比你想象的更频繁——如果你以为所有情况都服从那种漂亮、快速递减的正态分布的话。

cues.en: Because financial distributions
cues.zh: 因为金融领域的概率分布

cues.en: throw up unusual events more often than you would think.
cues.zh: 抛出异常事件的频率远超你的想象。

cues.en: And some of these things are hard to test for. And so we really want to have code that we really deeply understand,
cues.zh: 而其中有些情况很难通过测试覆盖。所以我们非常希望能有一套自己能真正深刻理解的代码，

cues.en: not just understand how it normally behaves,
cues.zh: 不仅要明白它平时的运行表现，

cues.en: but also
cues.zh: 还要

cues.en: understand its internals, understand the intent behind it. And so we kind of, as a company, view code not just as a way of getting things done, but also as a means of expression,
cues.zh: 理解它的内部机制，理解背后的设计意图。因此在我们公司看来，代码不仅是把事情做成的工具，也是一种表达方式，

cues.en: a way of saying what the system is supposed to do.
cues.zh: 一种用来阐明系统到底应该做什么的方式。

cues.en: Now, this shouldn't lead you to think
cues.zh: 但这不该让你以为

cues.en: that we only do this kind of correctness critical stuff. Like sometimes,
cues.zh: 我们只做这类关乎正确性的关键工作。有时候，

cues.en: you can go and read a paper about how NASA developed software.
cues.zh: 你可以去读一篇关于 NASA 如何开发软件的论文。

cues.en: And they do all this crazy stuff to make absolutely sure,
cues.zh: 他们做各种极端的事情来绝对确保，

cues.en: or almost
cues.zh: 或者说几乎

cues.en: absolutely sure, that nothing goes wrong in the rocket, because it's so expensive to get things wrong.
cues.zh: 绝对确保，火箭里不会出任何问题，因为出错的代价太高了。

cues.en: And then you think, that's really cool, but I'm not going to build my web crawler that way, because I don't care. It's like if there's a one in a million chance
cues.zh: 然后你会想，那真酷，但我不会用那种方式构建我的网络爬虫，因为我不在乎。就像如果有百万分之一的概率

cues.zh: 会发生可怕的事，那也没什么大不了的。

cues.en: And it's worth noting that not of
cues.zh: 值得注意的是，并非我们做的所有工作，

cues.en: the work we do, not all of the coding right, is correctness critical. A lot of it has
cues.zh: 也不是所有代码，都对正确性要求很高。很多时候，

cues.en: other more important things for it are things like speed to delivery. We do a lot of research coding. So we write our own research software, and there prototyping has a really big value. We write software for doing systems administration
cues.zh: 更重要的是其他因素，比如交付速度。我们会写很多研究代码，开发自己的研究软件，快速原型在这里价值很大。我们也会编写用于系统管理的

cues.en: in ML.
cues.zh: 机器学习代码。

cues.en: And again, it's
cues.zh: 再说一次，

cues.en: important that those things be correct, But there are so many sources of errors
cues.zh: 这些代码正确运行很重要，但普通的操作系统安装中有太多错误来源，

cues.en: in your average operating system install that making sure things are correct there is more about layering lots of different kinds of independent checks than it is about building one really, really solid executable.
cues.zh: 因此，要确保它们正确，关键是叠加许多不同类型的独立检查，而不是构建一个极其可靠的可执行程序。

cues.en: So there's a fairly wide diversity of different kinds of things that we do. One thing that is really different about our kind of shop for many shops is that
cues.zh: 所以我们做的事情种类相当繁多。我们这类团队和其他许多团队真正不同的一点在于，

cues.zh: 但是，

cues.zh: 我们不会去大量

cues.en: building of web UIs or GUI tool kits or
cues.zh: 开发 Web 前端或 GUI 工具包，也不会

cues.en: joining into
cues.zh: 去对接

cues.zh: 而且

cues.zh: 我们的另一个不同之处，跟一件长期以来困扰

cues.zh: 关心 ML 这类编程语言的人的事有关，就是：这语言到底为什么就是流行不起来？那些

cues.en: who like ML think it's wonderful, think it's the best
cues.zh: 喜欢 ML 的人觉得它棒极了，觉得它是构建软件的

cues.en: approach to building software, or at least one of the best approaches to building software.
cues.zh: 最佳方式，至少是最佳方式之一。

cues.en: And yet, it is
cues.zh: 然而，它却

cues.en: hilariously unpopular.
cues.zh: 出奇地不受欢迎。

cues.en: Nobody uses these languages. There are a very, very small minority

cues.en: programmer.
cues.zh: 程序员来说可能太难了。

cues.zh: 我也不确定这说法对不对。

cues.zh: 有些理由让人觉得确实如此，也有些理由让人觉得并非如此。

cues.en: more effective.

cues.zh: 那么，

cues.zh: 今天想讲的核心经验。接下来我会逐一分享几个小想法，并结合一些代码来演示。我想聊的第一个想法算是一种“元思考”，这又回到了我之前提到的，关于我们

cues.en: And one of the things I've noticed over the last eight years is that,
cues.zh: 过去八年里我注意到的一件事是，

cues.en: well, there are some people who work for us who spend a lot of their time, in fact, spend most of their time writing code. And there are some people who spend a significant fraction also reading the code of others.
cues.zh: 我们有些员工把大量时间、其实大部分时间都花在写代码上。还有些人也会花相当一部分时间阅读别人的代码。

cues.en: And there are systematic differences in opinion between the people who mostly write code and the people who spend lots of time reading code.
cues.zh: 而主要写代码的人和花大量时间读代码的人之间，在看法上存在系统性的差异。

cues.en: And I used to be a guy who mostly wrote code. And then as more people came on, I switched more to being a guy who mostly reads code. And one of the things I realized over time was that whenever there's a difference of opinion between these two groups, and there often is,
cues.zh: 我以前主要是写代码的人。后来加入的人越来越多，我就更多地变成了主要读代码的人。随着时间推移，我意识到，每当这两群人意见不合时——而这种情况经常发生——

cues.en: the readers are always right and the writers are always wrong. And
cues.zh: 读代码的人总是对的，写代码的人总是错的。而

cues.en: the reason for this is that, at least this is the case if
cues.zh: 原因是，至少在这种情况下，

cues.en: you're building something that's going to last, that multiple people are going to use, that's going to be shared. Because the interest of the reader
cues.zh: 如果你要构建一个能长久使用、会被多人使用、也会被分享的东西，那么读者的利益

cues.en: always pushes in the direction of clarity, simplicity,
cues.zh: 总是会推动代码变得更清晰、更简单，

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: moreover, that's kind of the ability to change the code later. And that's actually another thing I didn't mention, which is also very important in the kind of work that we do, is that we do lots of building of new systems, we do an enormous amount of changing of existing systems. Building software systems that can evolve
cues.zh: 也会让代码以后更容易修改。这其实是我刚才没提到的另一点，对我们做的这类工作也非常重要：我们不仅经常构建新系统，还要大量修改现有系统。要构建能够不断演进的软件系统。

cues.en: effectively and maintain correctness under that evolution is essential.
cues.zh: 在演进过程中保持高效并确保正确性，是至关重要的。

cues.en: And so whenever you see a trade off between
cues.zh: 因此，每当你需要在两者之间权衡：

cues.en: what would you like to do if you were the guy writing the code and what would you like to do if you were the guy who was forced to read the code, you should always in the direction of the reader.
cues.zh: 写代码的人希望怎么做，和被迫读代码的人希望怎么做，你永远应该偏向读者的利益。

cues.en: At least if the code if it's a throwaway thing that you're going to write a script and throw it away, maybe it doesn't matter because there won't be any readers. But in most real projects,
cues.zh: 当然，如果这只是随手写完就扔的一次性脚本，那可能无所谓，因为根本不会有读者。但在大多数实际项目中，

cues.en: code is read and changed
cues.zh: 代码被阅读和修改的次数，

cues.en: many more times than it is written. And so the reader's interests are paramount in that regard.
cues.zh: 远多于它被编写的次数。因此从这个角度来看，读者的利益是至高无上的。

cues.en: So now to something a little bit more concrete, creating uniform interfaces.
cues.zh: 现在讲点更具体的，创建统一接口。

cues.en: So in OCaml,
cues.zh: 在 OCaml 里，

cues.en: there's a thing called an MLI, which is this interface file which constrains
cues.zh: 有个叫 MLI 的东西，就是这种接口文件，用来约束

cues.en: the interface of the module that you write. So actually,
cues.zh: 你写的模块的接口。所以其实，

cues.en: is a two for one. There
cues.zh: 这是一举两得。这里

cues.en: are two pieces of advice here. One is create interfaces.
cues.zh: 有两条建议。一是创建接口。

cues.en: And again, this is one of these things between readers and writers. All the code I wrote at first, was like, interfaces.
cues.zh: 再说一次，这是读写双方之间的事。我最初写的所有代码，都像是接口。

cues.en: I'll write 80,000 lines of code and not put any interfaces anywhere, because I know what I'm doing. And it turns out, after a while, someone else has to read some of the code that you wrote. And the worst case scenario is when
cues.zh: 我会写 8 万行代码，一个接口都不写，因为我知道自己在做什么。结果过段时间，就得有人来读你写的代码。最糟糕的情况是，

cues.en: the jerk who's reading the code,
cues.zh: 那个读代码的混蛋，

cues.en: who doesn't understand what you did,
cues.zh: 不明白你当时做了什么，

cues.en: is you, because it's some time later and you've forgotten some details. And you don't know what you meant back six months ago when you wrote that. And boy, are you mad. Today, you is really mad at that old guy.
cues.zh: 而那个人竟然是你自己，因为时间过去了，你忘了某些细节。你也不知道六个月前写下那些代码时，自己到底想表达什么。天哪，你气坏了。今天的你，真是气坏了那个当年的自己。

cues.en: So even though it's tempting not to, if the project is expected to have any longevity, you should write interfaces.
cues.zh: 所以哪怕你很想省事，但只要这个项目需要长期维护，你就应该编写接口。

cues.en: And when you write interfaces, you should create uniform interfaces. You should have standards
cues.zh: 而且在编写接口时，应该保持接口的一致性。你们应该制定一套规范，

cues.en: about how interfaces should be built, and apply the standards uniformly to the code base. And again, is something again, you're writing a project for yourself, no one else is going to use,
cues.zh: 规定接口该如何构建，并在整个代码库中统一执行这些规范。话又说回来，如果你只是写个自己用、别人不会碰的项目，

cues.en: not as big of a deal. You're writing a project which you have 40 people who are going to be collaborating on, it's really important. Because having these uniform interfaces
cues.zh: 这倒无所谓。但如果你在写一个有 40 个人协作的项目，这就会非常重要。因为保持这些一致的接口，

cues.en: gives
cues.zh: 能建立起

cues.en: solid expectations that someone can take in to some new piece of code and use to quickly navigate and understand. It greatly increases
cues.zh: 明确的预期，让人在接触一段新代码时，能迅速理清头绪并看懂。这大大提高了

cues.en: the kind of
cues.zh: 那种

cues.en: flexibility
cues.zh: 灵活性

cues.en: and speed of people who are interacting with your code base.
cues.zh: 以及与你代码库交互的人员的速度。

cues.zh: 我容易讲得太快，大家完全可以随时提问。我

cues.zh: 马上就要做件可怕的事——往黑板上扔代码。然后一半

cues.zh: 的同学会看得一头雾水。没人会举手，接着他们就一直困在疑惑里。所以别这样。真的要提问。

cues.en: So what I want to pull up now is
cues.zh: 现在我想展示一个

cues.en: an example
cues.zh: 例子

cues.en: of a technique that we use for enforcing uniform interfaces.
cues.zh: 说明我们用什么技术来强制接口保持统一。

cues.en: And we basically do is we have interface components.
cues.zh: 基本上，我们会使用接口组件。

cues.en: So we write module signatures.
cues.zh: 我们编写模块签名。

cues.en: So if you look up there, at the top line it says module type comparable.
cues.zh: 看上面，第一行写着 module type comparable。

cues.en: So that declaration module type is basically the same thing as
cues.zh: 这个 module type 声明基本上和

cues.en: it's very similar to
cues.zh: 非常类似于

cues.en: the declaring what's in an MLI. It's declaring a signature.
cues.zh: 在 MLI 中声明内容，也就是声明一个签名。

cues.en: But here, unlike in MLI, where the MLI is kind of married to a particular implementation,
cues.zh: 但这里和 MLI 不同，MLI 通常和某个具体实现绑定在一起，

cues.en: this is a freestanding signature.
cues.zh: 而这是一个独立的签名。

cues.en: And the idea is that this signature sums up what it means for something to be comparable, for some
cues.zh: 这里的核心思想是，该签名概括了“可比较”的含义，

cues.en: type to support a comparison operation.
cues.zh: 即某种类型支持比较操作。

cues.en: And if you see, so there's three stanzas in here. The first stanza is a bunch of infix operators.
cues.zh: 大家可以看到，这里分成了三段。第一段是一组中缀操作符。

cues.en: The second stanza is a set of utility functions,
cues.zh: 第二段是一组工具函数，

cues.en: the most important one being the original compare one, which sort of sums up the basic ability to compare two things. And then the last two are actually module interfaces.
cues.zh: 其中最重要的是原本的 compare 函数，它基本概括了比较两个事物的基本能力。而最后两段实际上是模块接口。

cues.en: So these are now sub modules. So anything which is comparable has a submodule called map and another submodule
cues.zh: 所以这些现在是子模块。任何可比较的东西都有一个叫 map 的子模块，还有一个子模块

cues.en: called set, which use that comparison operator as the basis of a map type and a set type.
cues.zh: 叫 set，它们以那个比较运算符作为 map 类型和 set 类型的基础。

cues.en: So you can have one of these interfaces, and then you can use it.
cues.zh: 所以你可以拥有这些接口之一，然后就可以使用它。

cues.en: So here's an example of using multiple of these interfaces. The way it works is you say module car, so here colon sig. So now this really is like an MLI.
cues.zh: 下面是一个使用多个这类接口的例子。它的工作方式是，你写 module car，然后是冒号 sig。所以现在这真的很像一个 MLI。

cues.en: Sig to end is exactly like sticking an MLI
cues.zh: Sig 结尾的写法，就像是在 ML 文件顶部加一份 MLI

cues.en: on top of an ML file.
cues.zh: 文件。

cues.en: And so I declare there's a type T. And then I just say include comparable.
cues.zh: 所以我声明有一个类型 T，然后直接写 include comparable。

cues.en: And then there's a little bit of CRUP, with type comparable equals T.
cues.zh: 接着再加一点 CRUP，写上 type comparable equals T。

cues.en: This is how I force the types to unify
cues.zh: 我用这种方式让这些类型统一起来，

cues.en: in a clean way. It's actually an unfortunate miss feature of OCaml that I need this extra little bit of
cues.zh: 写得更简洁。OCaml 有个不太理想的缺陷：我需要多写这一小段

cues.en: verbiage to kind of unify the types away. And it's actually something that hopefully is going to be fixed in the next few revisions of the language to make this process a little bit smoother.
cues.zh: 代码，才能把这些类型统一起来。希望语言接下来的几个版本能修复这个问题，让整个过程更顺畅。

cues.en: But it's a little bit extra boilerplate, but you can basically do it. And then you have these standardized interface components. And there are two big wins from this. One of them is that it enforces standards.
cues.zh: 虽然要多写一点样板代码，但基本能搞定，这样你就有了这些标准化的接口组件。这会带来两大好处：其一就是它能强制推行规范。

cues.en: It's better than just telling people who work here, it's like, you really should follow this interface. It's like, no, you should just include this interface component. And then if you don't follow the interface, your code won't compile. There's
cues.zh: 这比单纯跟这里的同事说“你们真得遵守这个接口”有效得多；这相当于在说“不，你必须引入这个接口组件”，如果你不遵守接口，你的代码就编译不过。

cues.en: no better motivator than your code won't compile.
cues.zh: 没有什么比“代码编译不过”更能督促人了。

cues.en: And then the other thing is that
cues.zh: 还有一点是，

cues.en: this makes it much easier to use functors.
cues.zh: 这让函子的使用变得容易多了。

cues.en: So have functors been covered at all in this class? A little bit. Right. So the sort of very short, high level description of functors is functors are functions from modules to modules.
cues.zh: 这门课里讲过函子吗？讲了一点。对。函子的简短、高层次描述就是：函子是从模块到模块的函数。

cues.en: And when you have one of these functions, you kind of have to say in the signature of the function, what are you requiring of the input modules? And also, what you going to give on the output modules? You need to be able to specify the type signature. And you can use these same interface components when you're describing the thing that you expect from the module. And now, everyone who has fulfilled
cues.zh: 当你有这样的函数时，你得在函数签名里说明：你对输入模块有什么要求？还有，你在输出模块上要给出什么？你需要能指定类型签名。你可以用这些相同的接口组件来描述你对模块的期望。而现在，每个已经履行了

cues.en: the obligation of satisfying these interfaces
cues.zh: 满足这些接口的义务的人

cues.en: can also automatically
cues.zh: 也能自动地

cues.en: work along with that functor. And so the fact that everyone follows the same patterns
cues.zh: 配合那个 functor 一起使用。所以大家都遵循相同的模式，

cues.en: means its functors are much more broadly applicable with less work. Like otherwise, you have to do some sort of horrible
cues.zh: 意味着这些 functor 的适用范围广得多，需要做的工作也更少。否则，你就得做些糟糕的

cues.en: rejiggering of the module, like create a new module and pack things in in just the right pattern to fit the functor if things don't exactly match. And when you follow these standards, you have to do that a lot less.
cues.zh: 模块调整，比如新建一个模块，把各种东西按恰当的模式打包起来，才能适配 functor，尤其是原有结构不完全匹配时。遵循这些标准后，这类操作就少多了。

cues.en: And for what it's worth, when you see this map and set modules,
cues.zh: 顺便提一下，当你看到这些 map 和 set 模块时，

cues.en: in practice, those are actually created themselves by functors
cues.zh: 在实际应用中，它们本身其实也是由仿函数（functor）创建的，

cues.en: so that you don't have to actually redo the work of rewriting the map and set module every time you need it. You can create it in an automated way.
cues.zh: 这样你就不必每次需要时，都重新手写一遍 map 和 set 模块了。你可以用自动化的方式来创建它。

cues.en: All right, so uniform interfaces.
cues.zh: 好了，这就是统一接口。

cues.en: Here's another this is a really important one. Make illegal states unrepresentable.
cues.zh: 下面是另一个原则，这个非常重要：让非法状态无法被表示（Make illegal states unrepresentable）。

cues.en: What the hell does that mean? What that means is,
cues.zh: 这到底是什么意思呢？意思是，

cues.en: basically,
cues.zh: 基本上，

cues.en: the key benefit you get
cues.zh: 你获得的核心优势——

cues.en: well, there are a number of benefits. But one of the key benefits you get from a language like ML is that the type system
cues.zh: 嗯，优势有很多，但从 ML 这样的语言中获得的核心优势之一是：类型系统

cues.en: basically makes sure that various aspects of your program work properly
cues.zh: 基本能确保你程序的方方面面都正确运行，

cues.en: with a fairly small amount of effort from you.
cues.zh: 而且几乎不需要你费太大的力气。

cues.en: But the type system is not so wonderful that you can't defeat it. It turns out you can write your code badly
cues.zh: 但类型系统并没有那么神奇，你仍然可以绕过它。其实你可以把代码写得很糟

cues.en: in such a way that the type system doesn't give you very good guarantees.
cues.zh: 以至于类型系统无法给你很好的保证。

cues.en: There's a kind of self fulfilling prophecy that people who come to ML from other languages have, which they say, oh, well, all this really does is make sure that it's an int when I wanted an int. And then they write their code that way. And indeed, then all it does is make sure that you passed an int where you wanted an int. But anyone who becomes a halfway decent ML programmer has to learn to use the type system as a tool to
cues.zh: 从其他语言转到 ML 的人常有一种自我实现的预言，他们会说，哦，这其实只是确保我想要 int 的时候它是个 int。然后他们就那样写代码。结果确实，它只是确保你在需要 int 的地方传了个 int。但任何想成为还算合格的 ML 程序员的人，都必须学会把类型系统当作工具来

cues.en: enforce invariants, to enforce guarantees on the code that they write.
cues.zh: 强制不变量，对写的代码施加保证。

cues.en: And one of the key steps in doing that is choosing your data types in a way that
cues.zh: 实现这一点的关键步骤之一，是以这样的方式选择数据类型：

cues.en: whenever you can, whenever it's practical, that states that don't make sense, that are illegal,
cues.zh: 只要有可能，只要实际可行，就让那些不合理、非法的状态

cues.en: don't actually show up as legal states in your program.
cues.zh: 在程序中根本不会成为合法状态。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: let me again bring up an example here.
cues.zh: 我再举个例子。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: here is a little type definition
cues.zh: 这里有一个小小的类型定义，

cues.en: for an imaginary module for managing
cues.zh: 它属于一个虚构的模块，用于管理

cues.en: the state of a connection.
cues.zh: 连接的状态。

cues.en: So there are two types here to look at. The first one is a variant type.
cues.zh: 这里有两种类型要看。第一种是变体类型。

cues.en: In fact, it's a simple enumerated type. There are nothing inside the variants,
cues.zh: 实际上，它是一个简单的枚举类型。各个变体内部不包含任何内容，

cues.en: which just write down the three states that a connection can be in, connecting,
cues.zh: 只是写明了一个连接可能处于的三种状态：正在连接（connecting）、

cues.en: connected, and disconnected.
cues.zh: 已连接（connected）和已断开（disconnected）。

cues.en: And then we have this
cues.zh: 然后我们有这样一个

cues.en: record,
cues.zh: 记录类型（record），

cues.en: which is going to include the connection state as a subcomponent,
cues.zh: 它会把连接状态作为一个子组件包含进来，

cues.en: called connection info.
cues.zh: 名叫 connection info。

cues.en: And connection info has
cues.zh: 这个 connection info 是一个记录类型，

cues.en: a record of all the information that you keep
cues.zh: 里面保存了你所记录的

cues.en: about the state of the connection.
cues.zh: 关于该连接状态的所有信息。

cues.en: And there's a number of pieces here. You have the state, which just points back to that connection state type.
cues.zh: 这里有好几部分。你有状态，它指回那个连接状态类型。

cues.en: There's the server, which is the identity of the server that the connection is connecting to.
cues.zh: 还有服务器，即连接所连向的服务器的标识。

cues.en: There's the last ping time and the last ping ID. And the idea here is that in various protocols you have occasional pings that get sent out as a kind of keep alive mechanism.
cues.zh: 还有上次 ping 时间和上次 ping ID。这里的思路是，在各种协议中，你会不时发送 ping 作为一种保活机制。

cues.en: And here's where you store the last time that you got a ping and the last ID that you got,
cues.zh: 这里存储你上次收到 ping 的时间以及收到的上一个 ID，

cues.en: the idea of the last ping you received.
cues.zh: 也就是你上次收到的 ping 的思路。

cues.en: Then there's a session ID,
cues.zh: 然后是一个会话 ID，

cues.en: which is some identifier that's created when a new session is constructed.
cues.zh: 它是在创建新会话时生成的某种标识符。

cues.en: And then two times,
cues.zh: 然后还有两个时间，

cues.en: when initiated,
cues.zh: 一个是开始连接的时间，

cues.en: which has to do with when you started trying to connect. And again, this is for managing timeouts. The idea being if you started trying to connect and it's taking forever, you might want to give up and disconnect.
cues.zh: 它表示你何时开始尝试连接。同样，这是为了管理超时。如果你开始尝试连接后等了很久，可能就会想放弃并断开连接。

cues.en: And then when disconnected,
cues.zh: 还有断开连接的时间，

cues.en: so that if the connection gets terminated for some reason, as can happen for all sorts of exciting reasons, you keep track of the time that that happened.
cues.zh: 这样一来，如果连接因某种原因终止了（原因可能五花八门），你就能记录下它发生的时间。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: there's some good things to say about this. So first of all, it
cues.zh: 这也有一些优点。首先，它

cues.en: keeps track of a bunch of relevant information, which is nice. It's fairly readable.
cues.zh: 记录了一堆相关信息，这很不错。而且可读性也挺强。

cues.en: It's interesting that there's a lot of option types here, a lot of values that might be filled in and might not be filled in.
cues.zh: 有趣的是，这里用了很多 Option 类型，也就是很多可能填了、也可能没填的值。

cues.en: Now, you don't have to do that.
cues.zh: 不过，你也不一定非得这么做。

cues.en: If you're a working language like Java, you wouldn't do that. You would have them as nullable values.
cues.zh: 如果是在像 Java 这样的常用语言里，你不会这么写，而是直接把它们设成可空值（nullable）。

cues.en: And so you sort of stuff them in there. But maybe they'd be there, maybe they wouldn't. And you could discover by checking carefully, or maybe excitingly at runtime discover that something that you thought was going to be there wasn't.
cues.zh: 于是你就把它们塞进去。但它们可能在，也可能不在。你可以仔细检查来发现，或者更刺激一点，在运行时发现你本以为存在的东西其实并不存在。

cues.en: But this isn't really that much better than the Java version in the sense that there's a bunch of tricky little invariants
cues.zh: 但这其实并不比 Java 版本好多少，因为有一堆棘手的小不变式

cues.en: that kind of need to hold about this data. So for one thing, if you have a last ping time,
cues.zh: 需要在这个数据上成立。比如，如果你有一个 last ping time，

cues.en: you should probably also have a last ping ID.
cues.zh: 那你大概也应该有一个 last ping ID。

cues.en: And if you don't have a last ping time, you probably shouldn't have a last ping ID.
cues.zh: 如果你没有上次 ping 的时间，可能也不该有上次 ping 的 ID。

cues.en: And the session ID,
cues.zh: 还有会话 ID，

cues.en: you should really only have if you're connected.
cues.zh: 只有在连接时才应该有。

cues.en: And the when initiated, well, only if you're in the process of connecting does it make sense to keep that.
cues.zh: 至于发起时间，只有在正在连接时，保留它才有意义。

cues.en: And you have to be careful because you might end up

cues.zh: 你在用 ML 时遇到的很多磕磕绊绊，部分原因只是你还需要多学一些设计模式，掌握更多编写高效程序的思路。其实不用搞得这么花哨，你也能走得很远。但到了某个阶段，学习其中一些技巧就会变得非常值得。

cues.zh: 它们运作得很好。模块提供的抽象，

cues.zh: 因为对象抽象

cues.zh: 通常也最适合描述单个事物。

cues.zh: 但有时，你想抽象的是一组事物，以及它们之间的关系。有时这些事物属于同一类型，有时则属于不同类型，

cues.zh: 而模块是更自然的做法，

cues.zh: 如果用 C 来写，

cues.en: you often have to add abstractions anyway, because you can't actually get things done otherwise. Like go look at the implementation of GTK.
cues.zh: 你通常还是得加上抽象层，否则很多事情根本做不成。比如去看看 GTK 的实现。

cues.en: There's a big ass library. And they have their own special g object and all these. They have layers of cruft
